name: The Woman in the Locket
summary: Tamsin Tealeaf lifted a silver locket from a coach with no driver and no horses he could hear. The woman painted inside it has called his name in his dreams ever since.

stages.journal: Three months ago Tamsin lifted a silver locket from a nobleman's coach. Inside is a tiny portrait of a red-haired woman he has never met, and since that night she has called his name in his dreams from somewhere cold. He followed the dreams the way other people follow roads, and they brought him here.
objectives: Find out who the woman in the locket is

stages.journal: The woman in the locket has Ireena Kolyana's face: the same eyes, the same red hair, in a gown a few centuries out of fashion.

Her name was Tatyana. Strahd loved her; she loved his brother Sergei, and on their wedding day she went off the castle wall rather than be his. She keeps being born again in this valley, and Ireena is the latest.
objectives: Find out who put the locket where Tamsin's hand would find it

stages.journal: Behind the portrait, worn almost smooth: 'For T., from S. Every morning, at the water.' An S, but not the one on Ilse's letter. This one was written by someone who loved her and expected to be loved back.

The coach Tamsin robbed was Strahd's own black carriage, the one that goes about Barovia with nobody driving it. Last spring it was sent out through the mists, empty, the door on the latch and the locket on the seat. A thief would come, its master said. A thief always comes. Tamsin carried Tatyana's face home for him, exactly as planned.
objectives: Decide what becomes of the locket

stages.journal: At the Pool of the White Sun, Tamsin gave the locket back to the one who gave it first. Sergei's hand closed round it under the water, and the dreams stopped. Whatever Strahd meant the locket to do, it is out of his reach now, and the thief kept nothing for himself.

Tamsin put the locket in Ireena's hand. She looked at her own face, three hundred years old, and closed it gently, and said she'd keep it until she knew whose it ought to be. The dreams stopped. She has started remembering things.
Tamsin kept the locket. He says it's because he's a thief. He has also stopped opening it, and never lets it out of his hand at night.
objectives: Decide what becomes of the locket before the castle decides for you

stages.journal: In his own hall, Strahd held out his hand, and Tamsin put the locket in it. Strahd looked at the face inside for a long time and said thank you, as if he meant it, which was the worst part.
In the devil's own hall, with the devil watching, Tamsin dropped the locket into the fire. Strahd said nothing at all. It is the only time anyone has seen him with nothing to say.
